device.manufacturer: Pebble Technology (defunct 2016; revived via Rebble + Core Devices)
device.name: Pebble Smartwatch (Classic / Time / Pebble 2 / 2025 revival)
device.notes:
Pebble is the original crowdfunded smartwatch line (Classic, Steel, Time, Time Steel/Round, Pebble 2). Pebble Technology shut down in 2016 (IP to Fitbit then Google), but this is the model rescue story: in Dec 2025 Google open-sourced the PebbleOS firmware 100%, Core Devices ships new Pebble-compatible hardware, and the Rebble Foundation runs the web services and appstore. Full local control, no cloud.
APPLICATION LAYER — the "Pebble Protocol": endpoint-addressed packets. Every packet has a numeric `endpoint` and a body; framing is a length + endpoint prefix. Field types: Uint8/16/32/64, Int*, Boolean, UUID; four string encodings (PascalString length-prefixed, NullTerminated, Fixed, BinaryArray); structural fields Union/FixedList/PascalList/Embed/Padding/Optional. Default endianness is big-endian, configurable per field.
TRANSPORTS (libpebble2): direct Bluetooth serial to a paired watch; a WebSocket via the phone app's Developer Connection (port 9000); and QEMU for the emulator. Pebble supports only one simultaneous connection — disconnect the phone before connecting a computer over serial. No cloud is needed for protocol operation.
Endpoint NUMBER assignments beyond examples should be taken from libpebble2 source per message type.

openness.notes: libpebble2 was an official Pebble library, so much is documented rather than reverse-engineered; the firmware itself was open-sourced by Google in 2025. Rebble runs the appstore/web services; Core Devices ships new compatible hardware.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Watches advertise a "Pebble ..." name and pair as a standard Bluetooth device; there is no separate mode to enter from the client side.

pairing.notes: Ordinary operating-system Bluetooth pairing: the Pebble Protocol rides a serial link to an already-paired watch, so pairing is a precondition handled by the host stack rather than a step a client implements. Which association model the watch requests is not established here, and for a client it does not much matter — the pairing is done in the OS settings before any of this protocol starts.

credentials.notes: Standard Bluetooth pairing; no application-layer credential. No Wi-Fi on the watch itself.

factory_reset.description:
Two routes with different reach, and the button one is what matters for abandoned hardware: it works on a watch that is frozen, unresponsive or has no working phone app to drive the menu, which after the vendor's shutdown is most of them.
Button combinations differ across the range. Back, Up and Select together covers most models; the Steel is documented as Back and Select held for about ten seconds. Hold until the Pebble logo appears.
factory_reset.effect: Erases everything held on the watch — installed watchapps, settings and local data — and returns it to first-run state, so it must be paired and set up again.

steps.action: Hold Back, Up and Select together until the Pebble logo appears. On the Pebble Steel, hold Back and Select for about ten seconds.
steps.expect: The watch restarts to the Pebble logo.

methods.description: Pair the watch over Bluetooth, then speak the Pebble Protocol over one of the libpebble2 transports (Bluetooth serial to a paired watch, or a WebSocket developer connection on port 9000). Only one connection at a time.

steps.action: Connect via libpebble2 (Bluetooth serial, or the port-9000 WebSocket dev connection) and exchange Pebble Protocol packets.

setup.notes: Standard Bluetooth pairing; no vendor auth key. App installs now come from the Rebble appstore (apps.rePebble.com) and the mobile app can subscribe to multiple appstore feeds, so anyone can host a Pebble-compatible feed. High confidence: official library docs + the 2025 open-source release.

rejoin.notes: Re-pair over Bluetooth; no network membership to change.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The Pebble Protocol framing and libpebble2 transports are from the libpebble2 documentation; the 2025 open-source status from Core Devices / Google announcements.
